mission: Camp workspace, before dawn. Ben and Sera spread Codex notes between them and translate Ankhural's fragment into a practical shared-burden containment approach -- three Force traditions producing an emergent structure no single one can safely hold alone. Sera's archaic notation flows alongside Ben's modern Force analysis. Desh provides logistical reality checks.
why_now: The plan has to be built before sunrise or the timeline does not hold. The resonance note has to move from theory to tactics in the same room with the two people who will execute it.
conflict: The theory requires three distinct traditions — Sera's NSW discipline, Ben's modern-Jedi perception with Skywalker lineage, Kael's Sith training — combining without cancelling. It has never been tested, it might kill them, and it depends on a fourth person whose answer is not yet in.
turning_point: Sera adapts her archaic notation onto the shared-burden plan on its own terms. She is not translating Ankhural into her discipline; she is working the fragment as a live containment answer. Principled flexibility made visible.
opening_hook: Ben and Sera spread the Codex notes between them and work through the theory — both of them trying to stay ahead of what they're about to do.
closing_hook: The plan works — in theory. It requires three Force traditions. They have two who are willing. Kael is the variable. Without him, there is no resonance. Without resonance, there is only Torin's sacrifice or Veraine's destruction.
emotional_trajectory: Intense intellectual work -> breakthrough -> the dependency on Kael's choice

stakes.personal: Ben and Sera working as true partners for the first time
stakes.interpersonal: Sera moving from rigid certainty into principled flexibility
stakes.external: The resonance theory is the only alternative to Torin's unilateral sacrifice

turning_point_detail.trigger: Sera adapts her archaic notation onto the shared-burden containment plan on its own terms, working Ankhural's fragment as a live answer rather than translating it into her discipline.
turning_point_detail.shift: The dynamic between Ben and Sera pivots from parallel work to true partnership. Her willingness to hold her own tradition lightly while engaging the fragment's logic on its own terms signals a fundamental reorientation — not abandonment of NSW discipline, but integration of it into something larger.
turning_point_detail.cost: Ben recognizes that this partnership, this moment of genuine collaboration, now depends on a fourth person whose answer is not yet secured. The breakthrough carries immediate vulnerability: without Kael, the resonance collapses and the burden falls back onto Torin or the wound opens on Veraine's terms.

emotional_arc.start: Intense intellectual pressure — the need to solve an unsolvable problem before the timeline closes.
emotional_arc.shift: Breakthrough clarity when Sera's adaptation lands. The pressure transforms from abstract urgency into concrete possibility.
emotional_arc.end: Dependency and exposure. The plan is sound, but its execution depends on a choice Ben cannot control. The weight of that dependency settles into his awareness.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben and Sera spread Codex notes and archive data across every flat surface in the camp workspace, positioning themselves to work through the resonance theory side by side.
key_beats.state_change: The abstract pressure of the timeline becomes concrete. The problem is no longer theoretical — it is now a physical arrangement of fragments and calculations that must yield an answer.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Ben's instinct pushes toward action and forward momentum rather than explanation or doubt. His focus narrows to the work itself — the patterns in Ankhural's notation, the gaps in his own modern Force analysis, the shape of what might fit together. A low-level hum of urgency runs beneath his concentration.

key_beats.beat_description: Sera adapts her archaic NSW notation to match Ben's modern Force framework, her handwriting flowing alongside his on the same datapad. She is not translating Ankhural into her discipline; she is working the fragment as a live containment answer, holding her own tradition lightly enough to let the solution emerge.
key_beats.state_change: The collaboration shifts from parallel work to genuine partnership. Sera's flexibility is not compromise — it is disciplined engagement with a problem larger than any single tradition can hold. The resonance theory begins to cohere.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Ben's pressure tightens into focus. He registers the moment Sera stops defending her notation and starts using it as a tool. The shift is visible in her handwriting, in the speed of her adaptation, in the absence of hesitation. Something in his chest loosens slightly — not relief, but recognition that they are no longer working alone.

key_beats.beat_description: Desh provides logistical reality checks from the supply manifest while Ben and Sera calculate the resonance requirements — power draw, duration, the physical and Force-sensitive resources the containment will demand.
key_beats.state_change: The plan solidifies from theory into operational framework. The numbers are real. The requirements are clear. The path forward exists — but it has a condition.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Ben feels the weight of the dependency settle into place. The resonance requires three traditions. They have two. Kael is the variable, and Kael's answer is not yet in. The breakthrough carries immediate vulnerability. Without him, there is no resonance. Without resonance, there is only Torin's sacrifice or the wound opening on Veraine's terms. Ben holds both possibilities in awareness simultaneously — the plan that works and the plan that fails — and the gap between them is Kael's choice.
